name: Manu Bhaskaran
detail: Economist who analyzed wealth taxes but emphasized risks of capital flight and middle-class collateral damage; did not endorse an actual wealth tax

name: Tommy Koh
detail: Speaks frequently and passionately against economic inequality and for a fairer society, but has not advocated an actual net wealth tax

name: Singapore Democratic Party
detail: Policy platform calls for reinstating estate duties, luxury taxes, and raising top-1% income taxes, which fall outside the definition of an actual net wealth tax

name: Ravi Menon
detail: Former MAS Managing Director who proposed property gains and inheritance taxes in his 2021 IPS-Nathan lecture; did not advocate an actual net wealth tax

name: Kenneth Jeyaretnam
detail: Reform Party Secretary-General who opposed wealth taxes and argued wealth tax discussions were groundwork for GST hikes

name: Christopher Gee
detail: IPS Senior Research Fellow who authored research paper on Swiss wealth tax framing it as signalling mechanism with modest yield; did not endorse adoption

name: Chee Soon Juan
detail: Singapore Democratic Party Secretary-General whose economic platform focuses on reinstating estate duties and raising top-bracket income tax to 28% without proposing a net wealth tax

name: Paul Tambyah
detail: Singapore Democratic Party Chairman whose platform calls for restoring estate duty and progressive income taxation without proposing a net wealth tax

name: Lawrence Wong
detail: Prime Minister and Minister for Finance who rejected opposition proposals for a net wealth tax, stating net wealth taxes are difficult to implement without driving away mobile capital and cannot substitute for broad-based revenue

name: Singapore People's Party
detail: Opposition party whose manifesto 'It Is Time' calls for raising top-2% income taxes and reinstating estate duty, but does not propose an annual or net wealth tax

name: National Solidarity Party
detail: Opposition party whose manifesto 'Your Future, Our Priority' proposes progressive property taxes on multiple property owners and GST exemptions on essentials, but does not advocate a net wealth tax

name: Yip Hon Weng
detail: Member of Parliament for Yio Chu Kang SMC who cautioned against 'populist calls for wealth taxes' during the Budget 2022 debate, warning they create resentment and drive away talent and enterprise
